notes.heading: Optimise only inside the model's permitted domain
paragraphs: A quadratic's vertex is an unrestricted optimum on the real line when its curvature has the appropriate sign. A model may permit only a closed interval, whole-number inputs or times before a physical event. Evaluate the vertex only if it belongs to that domain, and otherwise compare the relevant boundaries. State the units of both input and output. A second mathematical root may be valid algebraically but outside a model's interpretation, so explain the exclusion instead of calling the algebra incorrect.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has perimeter 20 cm and width x restricted to 1≤x≤3 cm. Find the maximum allowed area.
solution: Length is 10-x, so A=x(10-x); the unrestricted vertex x=5 lies outside the interval.
A increases on [1,3], or compare its endpoint values 9 and 21.

questions.prompt: A fictional integer-output model is P(n)=-2n²+14n-8 for n∈{0,1,...,8}. Find every n giving maximum P.
questions.answer: n=3 and n=4 both give P=16.
solution: The real vertex lies at n=14/4=3.5.
Compare the neighbouring allowed integers; concavity makes them the best integer candidates.

questions.prompt: A fictional height model h(t)=5+8t-2t² uses metres and seconds. State the required units of 5, 8 and -2, and explain why the terms can be added.
questions.answer: 5 has units m, 8 has units m/s, and -2 has units m/s²; after multiplication by t or t², each term has units m.
solution: Every term in an equation for height must have height units.
Divide the required height unit by the appropriate power of time.
markingPoints: Give m/s and m/s² for the coefficients.
